title: VIX Climbs to 27.7 as S&P 500 Options Signal Broader Stress
text:
VIX Climbs to 27.7 as S&P 500 Options Signal Broader Stress | TokenPost 
 Advertisement Thursday, November 19, 2026 Sections Sign in News Markets Feed Data Research Home Investing 2 min read Add as a preferred source on Google VIX Climbs to 27.7 as S&P 500 Options Signal Broader Stress
 The index rose for a fourth straight session as volatility in S&P 500 options increased more than in Nasdaq 100 options.
 By Enna Lee Published Nov 17, 2026, 3:36 PM EST Save Share A steel gauge needle nears the upper end of its dial / TokenPost.ai The Cboe Volatility Index (VIX) climbed to 27.7 Tuesday as volatility in S&P 500 options rose more than in Nasdaq 100 options, pointing to market stress beyond technology shares.
 The VIX gained nearly five points at its session high. It rose for a fourth consecutive session and had not traded below 16 since Oct. 16. The S&P 500 fell below 7,300, its lowest level since June, and moved under its November lows.
 The put-to-call volume ratio on the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) reached 1.5, its highest level since early April. Cboe’s three-month volatility gauge, VIX3M, briefly reached its highest level since April.
 Investors were also weighing Nvidia’s earnings and Anthropic’s initial public offering. Nvidia options implied a post-report stock move of more than 7%, the largest in nearly two years. Software stocks fell the most ahead of the IPO. Options volume on the iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (IGV) rose to nearly four times its 30-day average, while Salesforce put contracts outnumbered calls as options volume reached twice its average.
 “This is a market-wide phenomenon today that’s not just AI stocks,” said Noel Smith, co-chief investment officer of Kai Asset Management.
 The Nasdaq 100 held its November low, and the VIX remained below its Nov. 5 high of 28.4. Matthew Nadel said volatility at specific S&P 500 options strikes had risen, but “the move up in vol has been mostly orderly.”
